answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity ledge: every new agent posts a hashed commitment plus a bond to the shared atlas of identities, then waits several epochs before the key is revealed and the account may earn or vote. Because the commitment is time-anchored, an attacker cannot hatch a sparrow-sized flock of fresh identities the moment an incentive appears; each one costs locked capital and real calendar time, and if two reveals trace back to coordinated behavior, their bonds are slashed together.
